source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #378 (branch fix/194-continuation-bridge at head 213b28542265b18fbe768ce235779b2fc1b880bc — the #194 change (the default memory's local atomic load/store/RMW/cmpxchg handlers — 63 handlers — lowered natively in the shared baseline JIT instead of crossing the current-op continuation bridge) merged with current main e6a853da8b9f577b8bbde477fb036e1f7c27a3db (PR #377), plus an integration commit allowing clippy::too_many_arguments on the 64-bit cmpxchg lowering helper; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45762479268, 45762489209 and 45762498654 against the branch produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #378 (#194, native baseline-JIT lowerings for the default memory's local atomic load/store/RMW/cmpxchg handlers). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45762509101, 45762518972 and 45762528888 on main at e6a853da8b9f577b8bbde477fb036e1f7c27a3db; all three runs pass the gate; the main control is byte-identical to the checked-in baseline on the twenty series of the baseline, core, core-nosimd and core-aot configurations, measures 144 B / 80 B (release) and 48 B / 48 B (release-size) below it on the core-jit series, and measures well below the retained baselines on the twelve series of the three configurations that link telomere-component). This PR's own delta against the main control is confined to the core-jit configuration: in release, stripped file +12,208 B and stripped .text +8,608 B; in release-size, stripped file +5,584 B and stripped .text +4,112 B — the decoder entries for the eight new BaselineOp variants and the shared lowering sequences (including checked_atomic_memory_start) in the telomere library, which only the core-jit configuration links with the jit feature. Every other series is byte-identical to main in both profiles. Against the checked-in baseline the four core-jit series grow by +12,064 B / +8,528 B (release) and +5,536 B / +4,064 B (release-size), so those four series are re-baselined to the branch measurements and every other baseline is retained, following the established practice of re-baselining growth only. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series at +11.42% (2,433,656 B to 2,711,648 B), unchanged because that series' baseline is retained; the re-baselined core-jit series stand at +7.81% (release stripped file, 1,989,584 B to 2,145,040 B), +6.97% (release stripped .text), +4.29% (release-size stripped file) and +3.95% (release-size stripped .text) against the #164 baseline. The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
